title: Scalar-compatible truncations and bounded standard structure at common stages
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Every $T_{L/E}$ is t-exact [def-weil-t-structure]. Its canonical comparisons with $\tau^{\le r}$, $\tau^{\ge r}$ and degree-zero cohomology $\mathcal H^r$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] are natural and satisfy the identity and composition equations with the specified scalar associators. On the pair category there is a bounded t-structure whose two halves and heart are the isomorphism closures of pairs $(E,K)$ with $K$ in the respective finite-stage half or heart. Truncation functors and their maps are induced by $(E,K)\mapsto(E,\tau_EK)$ and by conjugating finite-stage truncations of arrows by these canonical comparisons. These formulas are independent of representatives and descend all truncation-map equations and distinguished truncation triangles. In particular $\mathcal H^r(E,K)\cong(E,\mathcal H^r_EK)$, and every object in the common-stage heart becomes isomorphic to a degree-zero cohomology object at one finite enlargement of its coefficient field.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14; finite free scalar extension, coherent common-stage truncations and t-structure axioms

proof.text: The spectrum of the field $k$ has a single point and a finite affine cover by a Noetherian ring. Apply [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is Noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ remains a unit. Thus the integral and localized bounded t-structures [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure, prop-weil-localized-tstructure] apply at every finite coefficient field. Write $Q_E$ for localization and $C_{L/E}$ for integral change of completed coefficient rings. The construction of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] gives $T_{L/E}Q_E\cong Q_LC_{L/E}$; these are raw rationalizations throughout.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14(2); applicability to the completed finite-stage categories

proof.text: Put $R=B_{E,X}$ and $S=B_{L,X}$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is finite free as an $R$-module, and $C_{L/E}K=K\otimes_R^LS$ is already derived complete. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$, of size $d=[L:E]$, only for this calculation. For a K-flat resolution $P\to K$, restriction of $P\otimes_RS$ is the complex $P^{\oplus d}$, with componentwise differential. Kernels, images and quotients of this finite direct sum are the corresponding direct sums; hence $\mathcal H^i(P\otimes_RS)$, after restriction, is $\mathcal H^i(K)^{\oplus d}$. Restriction forgets scalar action and detects zero sheaves. Consequently $C_{L/E}$ preserves both ambient cohomological bounds. It preserves the constructible subcategories with their compatible etale-origin witnesses by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-constructible-scalar-transport]. By [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] it therefore preserves both integral halves. No levelwise truncation or Tor-compatibility assertion is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); finite-free change of completed coefficient rings and the cohomological bounds

proof.text: Every object of a rational half is isomorphic to $Q_EK$ for an integral object $K$ in that half [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Apply step 2 and $T_{L/E}Q_E\cong Q_LC_{L/E}$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Its image lies in the same rational half; shifts give this for every cutoff. This proves t-exactness, rather than merely exactness as a triangulated functor. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to obtain $c^-_{L/E,r}:T_{L/E}\tau_E^{\le r}\cong\tau_L^{\le r}T_{L/E}$ and $c^+_{L/E,r}:T_{L/E}\tau_E^{\ge r}\cong\tau_L^{\ge r}T_{L/E}$, characterized respectively by $\iota c^-=T(\iota)$ and $c^+T(\pi)=\pi$. This also gives their naturality in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), pp. 29–30; normalized comparison for a t-exact exact functor

proof.text:
For $E\subset L\subset M$, let $a:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}\cong T_{M/E}$ be the specified associator. The natural-transformation and composition clauses of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] give, for either truncation $\tau$,
$$c_{M/E,K}\,a_{\tau K}=\tau(a_K)\,c_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}\,T_{M/L}(c_{L/E,K}).$$
The identity comparison is the identity since $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$. These equations use exactly the associator of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Define the cohomology comparison by composing the upper and lower comparisons for $(\tau^{\ge r}\tau^{\le r}K)[r]$, followed by the iterated scalar shift comparison. This is the degree-zero cohomology object $\mathcal H^rK$ (the ambient sheaf when an integral representative is used) [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Substitution of the displayed equations and the associator/shift equations gives the identical identity and composition equations for $\mathcal H^r$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3 and definition 1.3.16; uniqueness and composition of normalized comparisons

proof.text: The comparisons identify the complete truncation triangles, including the third arrow. Indeed, apply $T_{L/E}$ to the finite-stage triangle at cutoff $r$, using its specified shift comparison [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Its first term has bound $\le r$ and its third term bound $\ge r+1$. The comparison equations in step 3 commute with the first two arrows to the standard truncation triangle of $T_{L/E}K$. For the first term $A$ of the source triangle and third term $B'$ of the target, $A[1]$ has bound $\le r-1$, so $\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],B')=0$ by [def-weil-t-structure]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension] now says that these prescribed first and third components, with middle component the identity, form a morphism of triangles: the boundary square commutes as well. The same uniqueness applies to cutoff-map diagrams; their finite-stage equations follow from the characterizing truncation maps, and remain valid under scalar extension.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(ii), pp. 29–30; Proposition 1.1.9 and Corollary 1.1.10(ii), pp. 23–24

proof.text: In the pair category [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], set the halves at cutoff $r$ to be the isomorphism closures of $(E,K)$ with $K\in D_E^{\le r}$ or $D_E^{\ge r}$, respectively. These classes have the required shift inclusions by their finite-stage counterparts and the pair shift [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. For orthogonality choose presentations of an upper object and a lower object with cutoffs $r$ and $r+1$. After conjugating by their chosen isomorphisms, any map is $[M,u]$ between their scalar extensions. Step 3 places its endpoints in the corresponding halves at $M$, so $u=0$ by finite-stage orthogonality [def-weil-t-structure, prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Thus the original map is zero. Each $(E,K)$ has the image of its finite-stage truncation triangle, distinguished because $j_E$ is exact [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. This supplies the triangle axiom. The two finite-stage bounds of $K$ give two bounds of $(E,K)$, proving boundedness. Thus these halves form the asserted bounded t-structure.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14(1),(2); explicit common-stage verification of t-structure axioms

proof.text:
Here is the actual descent formula; it does not apply an exact-functor descent assertion to truncation, which is generally not triangulated-exact. For either truncation put $\tau(E,K)=(E,\tau_EK)$. For $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ define
$$\tau(f)=[M,c_{M/F,L}^{-1}\,\tau_M(u)\,c_{M/E,K}].$$
If $M\subset N$, the associator equation of step 4 and naturality of $c_{N/M}$ show that transporting the displayed representative to $N$ gives exactly
$$c_{N/F,L}^{-1}\,\tau_N(a_{N,M,F,L}\,T_{N/M}(u)\,a_{N,M,E,K}^{-1})\,c_{N/E,K}.$$
The expression inside $\tau_N$ is $u_N$ by the pair-category definition. Thus two equivalent representatives give equivalent images. For composition, put both arrows at one stage [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]; the adjacent factors $c_{M/F,L}$ and $c_{M/F,L}^{-1}$ cancel, and $\tau_M(vu)=\tau_M(v)\tau_M(u)$. The identity formula follows from $c_{E/E}=1$. These calculations prove that both truncations are functors with the stated arrow formulas.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14; explicit conjugation and refinement calculation in the pair category

proof.text: Represent the upper counit on $(E,K)$ by $[E,\iota_{E,K}]$ and the lower unit by $[E,\pi_{E,K}]$. Their naturality for $[M,u]$ follows by substituting step 7 and the two characterizing equations of step 3. All equations between truncation maps are checked at a common finite stage using [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], where they are the ordinary finite-stage equations [prop-weil-localized-tstructure, def-weil-t-structure]. Step 5 handles the shifted third arrow of the distinguished truncation triangles, and [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms] sends each such finite-stage triangle to a distinguished pair-category triangle. These are truncation triangles for the halves proved in step 6. Their uniqueness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension](2), since the same upper/lower orthogonality gives its vanishing hypothesis in the pair category. Consequently the constructed functors are the canonical truncations of that t-structure, including all their canonical maps. Applying their composition and the pair shift gives naturally $\mathcal H^r(E,K)\cong(E,\mathcal H_E^rK)$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), pp. 29–30; common-stage descent of the units, counits and full triangles

proof.text: It remains to identify the heart; the witnesses for its two halves need not initially be at the same stage. Let $Z=(E,K)$ lie in both halves. Choose isomorphisms from $Z$ to a pair $(F,A)$ in the upper half and to a pair $(G,B)$ in the lower half. Include their inverses and both inverse equations in one finite diagram. By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] there is a finite $N\supset E,F,G$ where these are actual isomorphisms, so $T_{N/E}K\cong T_{N/F}A$ and $T_{N/E}K\cong T_{N/G}B$. Step 3 places the right-hand sides in the upper and lower finite-stage halves respectively. Hence $T_{N/E}K$ belongs to the finite-stage heart. Its two degree-zero truncation maps are isomorphisms, giving $T_{N/E}K\cong\mathcal H_N^0(T_{N/E}K)$ [def-weil-t-structure, prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. The canonical identification $j_NT_{N/E}\cong j_E$ [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms] now proves the required isomorphism for $Z$ after this one finite enlargement. Conversely every finite-stage heart object belongs to both pair halves. Therefore the pair heart is exactly the isomorphism closure of finite-stage hearts. No reflection of bounds by scalar extension or faithfulness of $j_E$ was assumed.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14(1),(2); simultaneous realization of the two heart witnesses

proof_origin.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14; completed finite-stage categories and explicit coherent common-stage argument, using BBD Proposition 1.3.3 and existing DAG interfaces. The paper does not state all coherence equations for this raw pair presentation.
